gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel system lamps, the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Every QSFP28 column carries a four-dot cluster above and below it and the SFP quad carries the same, but whether those four dots are four lanes, or link and activity for two ports, or something a NOS defines, is nowhere stated. The sixty-four lane-led-quad placements therefore keep the component's off/on default. The datasheet's own footnote - "NOS integration is necessary to activate the specific feature" - is about timing, not lamps, so it does not even license calling this nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The sixty-four numerals drawn on the port badges are placed from a measured badge position and numbered from the guide's annotation of the apertures - not read off the badges, which at fig-0015's 3.0 px/mm are two pixels of grey per digit. So the geometry is measured and the VALUES are inferred: what nobody has verified is that the badge over a column prints the same two numbers the guide writes inside that column's apertures. Every internal consistency check that can be run does pass - sixteen badges per band, two bulges each, one column each, and a numbering that closes at 63 - which is why they are drawn rather than left off. A single legible photograph of one block settles it.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front panel at 600 px per block or better, or a vendor mechanical drawing of the faceplate artwork

gaps.note: One orderable part number, FAN-803816-HI, dimensioned three different ways by three UfiSpace hardware guides. This device's Component Physical Information table says 81.5 x 122 x 81 mm (W x D x H); the S9600-30DX guide says 81 x 113 x 81.5, and ufispace/fan-803816@1 was built from it at a face of 82.5 x 81.5; the S9600-28DX guide says 80 x 113 x 81.5, and ufispace/fan-803816-hi@1 was built from it at 80 x 81.5. The depth alone varies by 9 mm, which is not a rounding. Measured on THIS device's rear elevation the bay pitch is 83.87 mm and the module 80.9 mm high, which supports this guide's 81 for the height and is silent about the other two axes. fan-803816-hi@1 is seated here because its name matches the SKU; the bay is authored 81.5 x 81.5 so the sibling also fits. No third component was minted for a part that already has two.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's own label, or calipers on a real FAN-803816-HI

gaps.note: Neither document names an orderable number for the chassis. The datasheet's "Available to Order" block lists only the FRUs - PSU-162-DESR, PSU-162-AESR and FAN-803816-HI - and the HIG names the product "S9600-64X" in its title, its overview and its dimensions table and prints no SKU anywhere. Searched both documents for the string 'S9600-64X-' and for any hyphenated suffix pattern; nothing. The AC and DC builds are listed as configurations without part numbers rather than invented, and note that the sibling S9510-28DC's SKUs (-BN0B / -BR1B) came from the owner and not from any PDF we hold, so a suffix guessed from that pattern would be a fabrication.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quotation naming the chassis SKUs

gaps.note: Searched and absent. The datasheet names the fan only as an ordering line ("FAN-803816-HI, exhaust air flow") with no wattage; the HIG dimensions and weighs the module (498 g) and tables its LED, and gives no power figure. Every watt figure in either document belongs to the box (565 typical, 1140 DC max, 1160.2 AC max), to a supply nameplate (1600, and the 1000-each 110 V derating) or to the provisioning reserve (1600 per circuit). L27/L29 stand for this module and the chassis total is a floor.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet

gaps.note: The guide states the count and the kind - five key-shaped attachment pins per side, ten in all, plus one M4x5.5 screw per side locking the inner rail - and draws them in Figures 9 and 10, but every one of those figures is an isometric of the chassis with a rail beside it and none is dimensioned or orthographic. The five drawn here are spread evenly over the middle 600 mm of the 762 mm depth with the screw behind the last: the number is sourced, the spacing is not, and it is almost certainly not even in reality since rail pins cluster where the standoffs land.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of either side wall, or a photograph of a side taken square on

provenance.attrs: datasheet SPECIFICATIONS/PERFORMANCE/ENVIRONMENTAL/REGULATORY tables, plus the HIG's Component Physical Information and Initial System Setup sections
provenance.bottom-face: estimated. No figure in the intake shows the underside. The compliance label is placed because the guide's regulatory section requires the markings and every chassis of this class carries them there; its position is invented and says so, and nothing else is drawn because nothing else is known. The face is otherwise symmetric left to right, which is recorded so the next reader knows the mirror was considered rather than skipped.
provenance.chassis: datasheet and HIG agree - 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm (W x D x H), 2RU, 19.15 kg without FRU. THE 436 IS THE BODY, NOT THE RACK FACE, and the guide says so in its own words: "the S9600-64X width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks". The ears are the difference between those two numbers and are not drawn. The 762 mm depth is likewise "without the field replaceable units": the guide adds that the fan handles project 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm beyond it, which is clearance to reserve and not chassis metal, so neither is in `depth`.
provenance.fan-module: SOURCES DISAGREE ABOUT ONE PART NUMBER AND THE LIBRARY ALREADY HELD TWO ANSWERS. This device's own Component Physical Information table gives the fan 81.5 x 122 x 81 mm (W x D x H); the S9600-30DX guide gives 81 x 113 x 81.5 and the S9600-28DX guide 80 x 113 x 81.5 - three tables, one SKU, FAN-803816-HI. Rather than mint a third component for the same orderable part, ufispace/fan-803816-hi@1 is reused and the disagreement filed. What was measured HERE, on this device's own figure, is a bay pitch of 83.87 mm and a module height of 80.9 mm (the seams at 64 and 302 px), which matches this guide's 81 rather than the component's 81.5 - by 0.6 mm, or 1.8 px at this figure's scale. The bay is authored 81.5 x 81.5 so that either sibling component seats in it.
provenance.front-layout: drawing - HIG Figure 8 "Port Overview" (extracted as fig-0015), the only orthographic front elevation in the intake. GATE 1: its front face measures 1308 px wide by 258 px high against a stated 436 x 87.7 mm, an aspect of 5.07 against a true 4.97, so it is within 1.6% and carries geometry. Scales used throughout: 0.333333 mm/px in x from a face left edge at 3.5 px, 0.33992 mm/px in y from a face top edge at 49.5 px. THE VERTICAL SCALE IS THE SOFT ONE. The figure's left edge measures 255.4 px tall and its right edge 260.0 px - the bottom edge slopes about six pixels across the panel - so 258 px is the mean of the two and every y here carries roughly +/-0.4 mm that no number of decimal places will remove. The x scale has no such ambiguity: both vertical edges are crisp and the width is the datasheet's.
provenance.grounding: drawing - HIG Figure 7 and the guide's section 8. The grounding location is on the REAR, between the fan bank and the supplies, and ships "covered with a protective label"; the figure draws a light 10.1 x 35.1 mm plate with two 7.9 mm bolt circles on it, an earth symbol to its right and a small tab circle below. Modelled as decor plus a ground-symbol placement: the lug itself (29 x 37.5 x 12.5 mm, #6 AWG, two M4 screws) is a loose accessory in the carton and is not fitted, so nothing is drawn for it.
provenance.led-semantics: HIG section 10 "Verifying System Operation", Front Panel LED table, transcribed in full rather than cited. SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID each carry their own vocabulary and two of them separate meanings by BEHAVIOUR rather than colour, so a state carries a behavior as well as a color. The same section's PSU FRU and Fan FRU tables belong to those modules and are transcribed in their contracts. THE GUIDE GIVES NO TABLE FOR THE PORT LAMPS, so the sixty-four lane-led-quad placements keep their component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary - see the port-led-semantics gap.
provenance.paint-bands: drawing-measured by colour. The QSFP area carries an olive band above and below the cages - #556c3c at the top, rendered #445338 in shadow at the bottom, one colour - from 68.5 to 91.5 px and 272 to 287.5 px, and it is what the lamps and the row arrows are printed on. Over the SFP quad and the FIRST QSFP column that band is YELLOW (#e0dd4a, 163.5 to 344 px) with an ORANGE sub-band (#b85c2c, 277 to 344 px) under its lower half. That is the vendor's own convention stated in the guide's Port Overview - "the ports 0 to 3 (labelled in yellow) breakout from the 100G port 0 (labelled in green)" - except that the yellow reaches over QSFP port 0's lamps as well as the SFP quad's, which is the marking of the shared port. Drawn as measured; the reason the orange stops where it does is not explained by any text we hold.
provenance.port-numerals: drawing - the panel prints a white pointed badge just outside each port column on each paint band, and the badge carries that column's TWO port numbers stacked, the upper row's over the lower row's. Sixteen per band: seven pairs at the internal block boundaries plus one at each end of the array, at 9.67 mm outboard of each column centre, a model that lands on all nine detected white runs to within three pixels. THIS WAS READ WRONG FIRST AND THE CORRECTION IS WORTH KEEPING. At 24x the badge's pointed ends look exactly like a stacked up-arrow and down-arrow with something illegible between them, and a first draft of this file modelled them as arrows and filed the middle glyph as unreadable. What overturned it was a sibling model of the S9600-32X being built from the same vendor's artwork at the same time, which read the same shape as a number badge; going back to a 30x crop with that in hand shows the badge has TWO bulges, each holding a pair of grey glyph blobs - two digits over two digits, which is not an arrow. Column 0's TOP badge is not white: it falls on the yellow and orange bands and the ink is printed straight onto them, dark over the yellow and light over the orange, which is what the black-triangle-over-white-triangle at 283-291 px actually is. THE DIGITS THEMSELVES ARE NOT READ OFF THE BADGE - at 3.0 px/mm they are two pixels across - and they are not a guess either: the guide's own Port Overview annotates every aperture, so the numbering is sourced and only the ink's position is measured. See the port-numeral-ink gap for what that leaves open. The large numerals Figure 8 prints INSIDE each aperture are a different thing and are not drawn. They sit over the module faces at a size no faceplate prints, neither the datasheet's front render (fig-0003) nor either product photograph shows them, and they are the guide annotating its own drawing. Contrast s9510-28dc, where the numerals ARE panel paint, on a coloured band outside the aperture, and are drawn.
provenance.power: datasheet for the typical, HIG for the maxima, and the three are NOT one number stated three ways. The datasheet gives "Typical power: 565 Watts (no transceiver)" - explicitly a bare box. The guide's Connecting Power sections give 1140 W maximum on DC and 1160.2 W on AC, each followed by its own criteria block: 45 C, optics fully populated, 100% traffic load. `power-envelope: as-tested` names those criteria, which is what the maxima carry; the typical is a different envelope and cannot share the key, so its scope is written into its own value. The 1600 W per circuit in the installation requirements is supply to be provisioned, not draw, and is filed as `power-reserve-per-circuit-w` so it can never be summed with the others.
provenance.psu-default: THE BAYS DEFAULT TO THE AC SUPPLY BECAUSE THAT IS THE BUILD THE GUIDE DRAWS. Figure 7's rear elevation - the only rear elevation in the intake, and the one every number on that face is measured from - shows a C20 appliance inlet on both supplies, which is the AC unit. The vendor's prose leads with DC in both documents ("1. DC Version ... 2. AC Version", and PSU-162-DESR before PSU-162-AESR in the ordering block), so leading with AC here is a choice and not a reading of the vendor's preference: it is the build that can be checked against a picture, and the DC build is a configuration one click away. Both supplies are real orderable parts and neither is more correct; what would be wrong is defaulting to the one no held figure shows and then comparing the render with a figure of the other.
provenance.psu-module: ufispace/psu-162-ac@1 and psu-162-dc@1 reused unchanged - same SKUs (PSU-162-AESR / PSU-162-DESR, named in this datasheet's own Available to Order block) and the same 50.5 x 360 x 40 mm the Component Physical Information table gives here. That is an agreement between two guides rather than an echo of one: this device's table and the S9600-30DX table were read separately and give the same three numbers.
provenance.qsfp-block-shell: drawing - the bright bezel frame each ganged block presents is PANEL METAL and is drawn as `panel.decor`, not as part of any port. Skip it and sixty-four dark apertures sit on a dark faceplate and vanish; it is the single most repeated by-eye finding in this library. Sized from the measured block outlines (40.33 mm wide) and the two assembly bands (30.42 and 30.25 mm tall), filled #c9cdd1 - the figure renders the metal at about #dcdfdf under its own highlight, which is lighter than sheet metal reads on a faceplate, so the library's connector-shell grey is used instead and the figure's value recorded here.
provenance.qsfp-pitch: drawing-measured FROM THE LAMPS, NOT THE CAGE FILLS. Each QSFP28 column carries a four-lane lamp cluster above it and another below, and those clusters repeat once per PORT, which the filled grey rectangles in the figure do not - those are module faces. Colour-detecting the lamp dots on the lower band gives sixteen cluster centres whose within-block separation averages 56.69 px (18.90 mm) and whose block-to-block pitch is 126.2 px (42.067 mm) over a least-squares fit across all eight blocks. 18.90 is the TE 2322551-4 ganged pitch of 19.00 to within a tenth of a millimetre, so the standard number is used and the block is anchored on its measured midpoint rather than accumulating the difference sixteen times. Cross-checked independently: thresholding the row-1 band gives eight bright block outlines 122-124 px wide on left edges 283, 411, 537, 665, ~791, 914, 1040 and 1169 px, and block 1's own midpoint of 343.5 px predicts port centres at 315.0 and 372.0 against the 314.75 and 372.5 the lamps give.
provenance.qsfp-rows: drawing-measured at 10x on fig-0015. A block is two stacked 2-high ganged assemblies with a dark seam between them: the upper assembly runs 92 to 181.5 px and the lower 182.5 to 271.5, and within an assembly the two apertures are belly-to-belly with the EMI band of the upper row below it and of the lower row above it - which is why rows 2 and 4 carry `rotate: 180`. Aperture centres at 112.5, 160.25, 203.0 and 250.75 px give row tops of 16.62, 32.85, 47.38 and 63.61 mm, an in-assembly row pitch of 16.23 mm and an assembly pitch of 30.76 mm. The 9.58 mm opening height is the standard's, not the figure's: the drawn apertures measure 27-28 px, which is 9.1-9.5 mm and cannot resolve the difference.
provenance.rear-layout: drawing - HIG Figure 7 (fig-0014) rear elevation. Its face measures 1293 x 258 px against 436 x 87.7 mm, an aspect 0.8% from true, so 0.33720 mm/px in x from a left edge at 52 px and 0.33992 mm/px in y from a top edge at 54 px. The fan bay pitch is measured from two features that each repeat once per bay and agree: the status lamps at 110.0, 358.9, 607.5 and 856.3 px and the red 'E' airflow badges at 102.1, 351.1, 600.1 and 848.9 px, both a 248.8 px pitch, i.e. 83.87 mm. The PSU bays are read from their own borders - 1155-1305 px wide (50.6 mm, against a tabled 50.5) and 63-181 and 189-306 px tall (40.1 mm each, against a tabled 40.0).
provenance.sfp-quad: drawing-measured at 8x. The four SFP28 cages sit in one 2x2 ganged block whose outer frame runs 163.1-255.6 px by 96.3-176.3 px, i.e. 30.83 x 27.20 mm. Two ports at the SFF-8433 14.25 mm pitch plus the 1.2 mm the standard gives the block's own bezel is 30.9 mm, which is the frame to a tenth, so the standard pitch is used and the pair anchored on the frame's midpoint. The row pitch is taken from the two aperture TOPS - 97.5 and 141.9 px, 15.09 mm - and not from the separator between them, which is where a first reading got 13.6 mm by measuring to the wrong edge; 15.09 is std/sfp-ganged's own documented 15.00 belly-to-belly. Rows mirror, same as the QSFP block.
provenance.side-faces: estimated, and the axis convention is stated because it is the one that bites. On a RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT; on a LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, so the same pin at 80 mm from the front sits at x 80 on the right and x 679 on the left. The guide states the COUNT and the KIND - "the chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins" plus one M4x5.5 screw hole per side for the inner rail - and Figure 9/10 draw them, but no figure dimensions them and no figure of a side is orthographic. The five are therefore spread evenly over the middle 600 mm and the screw placed behind the last one; the count is sourced, the positions are not. See the rail-pin-positions gap.
provenance.system-lamps: drawing-measured at 14x - a white legend block at 24.4-38 px by 216.4-263.9 px with the six lamps in a column immediately right of it at 39.1-50.1 px. The drawn lamp pitch is 7.5 px (2.55 mm) and common/led-rect is 2.6 mm tall, so the six are laid out on a 2.6 mm pitch centred on the measured strip centre - 0.5 mm taller than the figure over the whole stack, which is one and a half pixels there, and the alternative was six lamps overlapping each other by a hair.
provenance.top-face: drawing - the top elevation in HIG Figure 4 (fig-0010, left panel) shows six full-length stiffening grooves. That figure's plate measures 390 x 650 px against 436 x 762 mm, an aspect 5% from true, so only fractions along each axis are taken from it: the grooves are read at 105 mm pitch starting 131 mm behind the front edge, each about 20 mm across. y = 0 is the FRONT on this face.
